sources.quote: Just off Gadem Lam, on the hillside above Trashi Chho Dzong, this small, friendly nunnery has links to Thangtong Gyelpo
Zilukha is a northern district, located between Jungshina to the north and Sangyegang to the south.

facts.rationale: Lonely Planet POI page (quote verified at the canonical POI URL; A's old URL now redirects to a generic Bhutan page) puts it on the hillside above Trashi Chho Dzong; Wikipedia places it in Zilukha, Thimphu; no T1 contradiction.

sources.quote: Thangtong Gyalpo (1385 CE–1464 CE

facts.rationale: 1385-1464 is the 15th century.
'One of the few active nunneries in Bhutan' is unsourced and probably overstated (Bhutan has many nunneries); daily pujas are not documented by a reliable source.

sources.quote: Drubthob Goemba (now the Zilluka nunnery)
It contains the Drubthob Gonpa/Zilukha Nunnery once belonged to the Drubthob (Realized one) Thang Thong Gyalpo

facts.rationale: Wikipedia equates Drubthob Goemba with the Zilukha nunnery, linked to Thangtong Gyalpo.

sources.quote: 'Anim Dratshang' in Thimphu located at Zilukha
It contains the Drubthob Gonpa/Zilukha Nunnery once belonged to the Drubthob (Realized one) Thang Thong Gyalpo

facts.rationale: Restates identity: a nunnery (anim dratshang) in Thimphu.

sources.quote: It contains the Drubthob Gonpa/Zilukha Nunnery once belonged to the Drubthob (Realized one) Thang Thong Gyalpo
Thangtong Gyalpo (1385 CE–1464 CE

facts.rationale: Only numeric differed: '15th-century' is a date claim, so numeric=true; Wikipedia Thimphu ties the nunnery to Thang Thong Gyalpo (1385-1464).
No reliable source gives the nuns' school; the nunnery is linked to Thangtong Gyalpo's lineage, and the Drukpa Kagyu affiliation is unconfirmed.

sources.quote: 'Anim Dratshang' in Thimphu located at Zilukha
We have around 50 nuns and our nunnery welcomes people of all cultures and faith.

facts.rationale: A nunnery (Anim Dratshang) at Zilukha, Thimphu.

sources.quote: Just off Gadem Lam, on the hillside above Trashi Chho Dzong, this small, friendly nunnery has links to Thangtong Gyelpo
It contains the Drubthob Gonpa/Zilukha Nunnery once belonged to the Drubthob (Realized one) Thang Thong Gyalpo

facts.rationale: Lonely Planet (verified at canonical POI URL): hillside above Trashi Chho Dzong, i.e. above the valley floor in the Thimphu valley; Wikipedia confirms it is in Thimphu.
Hillside above the city is supported, but 'wooded' and 'western edge' are not; Wikipedia places Zilukha in northern Thimphu.
No reliable source confirms a Drukpa Kagyu affiliation.

sources.quote: Thangtong Gyalpo (1385 CE–1464 CE

facts.rationale: Thangtong Gyalpo lived 1385-1464 (15th century), not the 19th.

sources.quote: We have around 50 nuns and our nunnery welcomes people of all cultures and faith.

facts.rationale: A nunnery, i.e. a monastic house for nuns.
No reliable source describes a central lhakhang used for communal ceremonies.

sources.quote: traditional Bhutanese building structures in Thimphu are the Tashichho Dzong, Drubthob Goemba (now the Zilluka nunnery)
We have around 50 nuns and our nunnery welcomes people of all cultures and faith

facts.rationale: Wikipedia lists Drubthob Goemba (now the Zilluka nunnery) among Thimphu's most prominent traditional buildings; The Bhutanese (2017) quotes a senior nun: around 50 nuns, learning Buddha's teaching. Wikivoyage (B) not used.
No reliable source gives a founding year; a local blog says the temple was built 1981-1983, which conflicts with 1976 but is not a reliable source.

sources.quote: It contains the Drubthob Gonpa/Zilukha Nunnery once belonged to the Drubthob (Realized one) Thang Thong Gyalpo

facts.rationale: Linked to Thangtong Gyalpo, whose dates are 1385-1464.

sources.quote: 'Anim Dratshang' in Thimphu located at Zilukha has become a popular tourist destination
One tourist visiting the Anim dratshang questioned why the nunnery had male gods

facts.rationale: The Bhutanese uses 'Anim Dratshang' at Zilukha interchangeably with 'the nunnery' (quotes verified on page); T2, no T1 contradiction.

facts.rationale: Wikipedia puts the nunnery in the Zilukha district; Lonely Planet (verified at canonical POI URL) says hillside above Trashi Chho Dzong.
No reliable source mentions a tradition that Thangtong Gyalpo meditated at this site.

sources.quote: Zilukha is a northern district, located between Jungshina to the north and Sangyegang to the south.
Motithang is a north-western district of Thimphu.

facts.rationale: Wikipedia Thimphu: the nunnery is in Zilukha (northern district, north of Sangyegang), while Motithang is a separate north-western district south of Kawajangsa, so 'above Motithang' is wrong; 'overlooking the valley' is a view claim (trip_leak).
A generic description of temple and residences; no reliable source.
A generic description of temple and residences; no reliable source.
Drukpa Kagyu is Bhutan's dominant school, but no source confirms this nunnery belongs to it.
Wikipedia only says it is a traditional Bhutanese building; 'whitewashed walls and a central temple' not found in a reliable source, so unverifiable (same rule as other partly-sourced facts).
